To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and demonstrated a 64× time-interleaved 2.5GS/s 10-bit ADC in 65nm CM OS that achieves 48.5-dB SNDR at Nyquist frequency with only 0.480W power consumption.
a time-interleaved 2.5GS/s 10bit ADC in 65nm CMOSTM technology is presented that achieves a 48.5-dB SNDR and 0.48-W power consumption.
a 2.6GHz 10b 480mW ADC is demonstrated with 48.8dB SNDR and 48.5 dB SNDR at Nyquist, and a novel open-loop buffer array architecture is presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a low-power, low-cost, and high-performance ADC for TV-band applications.
the development of an ultra-low power, ultra-high speed ADC that can be used for cable TV reception.
the development of an ultra-low-power ADC that can be used for the digitization of the entire TV band, with a view to the integration of a baseband DSP on a single chip.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed ADC achieves the highest reported SNDR in a single-channel 2GS/s 65nm CMDS ADC, while consuming the lowest power in a single-channel and a 2GS/s ADC.
this work demonstrates a 2.6 GS/s time-interleaved 10b ADC in 65 nm CMOS with a power efficiency of 480mW/10b, which is the best reported to date.
the presented architecture is the first 10b ADC to achieve Nyquist SNDR in excess of 45dB with a power consumption below 1W.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new ADC architecture, which can digitize the TV band with 10b and 2.6 GS/s at a low power consumption of 0.48 W.
we have achieved the highest reported SNDR and the lowest reported power for 10b ADCs at 2.6 GS/s.
a high-resolution ADC is not required for cable TV applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the interleaving hierarchy can be used to simplify the ADC design, and that the feedforward-sampling mode is a viable alternative to the conventional feedback-sampling mode in the interleaving hierarchy.
the interleaved ADC can be operated in feedforward sampling and feedback-SAR modes to achieve high speed and power efficiency.
the interleaving hierarchy can be extended beyond two stages to achieve a high sampling speed with a low power consumption.
